name: Centro (Historico)
tagline: Colonial core around Plaza 9 de Julio
description: The historic heart around Plaza 9 de Julio, with colonial churches, museums, the cathedral and arcaded streets. Home to most hotels, restaurants and services, it is walkable and central, lively by day and evening, though busy and pricier than outer districts.
bestFor: Nomads wanting walkable access to cafes, museums and services

name: Balcarce
description: The area along Calle Balcarce north of the centre, famous for its penas (folk music venues), bars and restaurants near the old train station. It is the nightlife hub, buzzing after dark with live Andean music, and a short walk from the centre.
bestFor: Social travellers wanting live folk music, bars and dining out

name: San Lorenzo
tagline: Leafy green suburb in the hills
description: An upscale green village about 10km west of the centre, set against forested hills with a cooler microclimate. Known for its shady quebrada walk, gardens and quiet residential streets, it offers a relaxed retreat but needs a car or bus for the city.
bestFor: Remote workers wanting quiet green surroundings and cooler air

name: Barrio Tres Cerritos
tagline: Quiet residential area northeast of centre
description: A well-regarded residential neighbourhood northeast of the centre, with tree-lined streets, parks, cafes and some of the city's nicer housing. Safe and calm with everyday shops nearby, it suits longer stays wanting a settled local feel close to the city.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a safe, quiet residential base near the city
